clue.text: Frenchman's overwhelmed by a leading Christian message

indicators.note: leading says the Christian abbreviation goes at the front of the message

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for Christian
a cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire

explanation.surface: Someone is moved by a prominent Christian sermon or announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenchman's overwhelmed' means the French word for overwhelmed, as a Frenchman would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French past participle accablé translates as crushed or overwhelmed.

clue.text: A bounder holding man up in pub

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other inside it

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person, a cad or bounder

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: he is the pronoun standing for a man

explanation.surface: A cad is propping a fellow up in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a tavern or public house serving beer.

clue.text: Mexican composer (1828-1900) disturbed Grecian muleteer

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of these two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A troubled Greek mule driver, set beside the name of a Mexican composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemente Aguirre was a nineteenth-century Mexican musician known for waltzes and church music.

clue.text: Trendy musicians outside came into view in south coast resorts

indicators.note: outside means the musicians' word wraps around the trendy word

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
right-on means fashionably progressive, trendy
hove is the old past tense of heave, as in a ship that hove into view

explanation.surface: A fashionable band appears outdoors at seaside towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton and Hove are neighbouring towns on England's Sussex coast, now a single city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both towns are seaside holiday destinations on the English Channel coast.

clue.text: To win, avoid scrambling!

parts.note: the winner of this school sports-day event must not drop the egg balanced on a spoon, so it must not get scrambled

explanation.surface: Advice that rushing about will cost you victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambling' reads as hurrying, but it means breaking the egg; a race where children carry an egg on a spoon is a British sports-day staple.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's race, dropping and smashing the egg loses, so success depends on keeping it whole.

clue.text: Non-drinker cares about Manx tournament

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is worried about an event on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, whose people are Manx, hosts the famous Tourist Trophy motorcycle road races.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man Tourist Trophy is an annual motorbike racing competition held on public roads.

clue.text: A pest of Nazareth represented as feral child in literature

indicators.note: represented as means these letters are presented again in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A nuisance from Nazareth is portrayed as a wild child in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs's 1912 novel tells of a boy raised by apes in the African jungle.

clue.text: 1964 horror fantasy film of Lazio playing the A.S. team?

parts.note: SS Lazio is a football club based in Rome
a team playing another is up against it
AS Roma is the other Rome football club

explanation.surface: A film title imagined as a Roman football derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rome derby pits Lazio against AS Roma, both clubs from the same city, so the match is literally one Rome side versus another.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1964 American picture, also called War of the Zombies, mixes horror with sword-and-sandal fantasy.

clue.text: Singer with monocycle ruined the last part of the Olympics

definitions.text: the last part of the Olympics

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A vocalist on a unicycle spoils the end of the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The Games end with a closing ceremony of parades, music and the handover to the next host city.

clue.text: Braised and well-oiled

definitions.meaning: cooked slowly in liquid in a covered pot

explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked slowly in liquid is stewed, and stewed is also slang for thoroughly drunk.

clue.text: Herbal remedy still popular with grand prissy girl

parts.note: even and still both intensify, as in even better or still better
in means fashionable or popular
G is short for grand, a thousand
prim means primly fussy, prissy
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A natural remedy is still favoured, along with a grand, starchy young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from the seeds of this yellow wildflower is sold as a herbal supplement.

clue.text: Intimate tango he performed systematically?

indicators.note: performed means these letters are acted out in a different sequence

explanation.surface: A man dances a close tango in a careful, ordered way.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing tasks singly, in turn, is working in an orderly, step-by-step manner.

clue.text: Carry On actress comes round one short month backing Cheers and Miranda

indicators.note: comes round means the actress's name is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: Joan Sims appeared in many of the British Carry On comedy films

indicators.note: backing means the month abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October

explanation.surface: An actress from the Carry On films visits and cheers someone named Miranda.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were a long run of British slapstick comedies. Cheers is an American sitcom and Miranda a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are examples of situation comedies, television shows built around a fixed set of characters.

clue.text: Fruit — love what's on offer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a range is the selection of goods a shop offers

explanation.surface: A fond look at what the fruit stall is selling.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit with a tough peel and sweet segments.

clue.text: Grasp what reels have

definitions.meaning: to understand or catch on to something
reels of thread carry cotton wound on them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to begin to understand, and it also literally describes thread wound on a spool.

clue.text: Tried and gained control in the past

parts.note: to have had something is to have got hold of it
ago means back in time, in the past

explanation.surface: Someone attempted it and once took charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having made an attempt at something.

clue.text: Messenger into fruit

parts.note: read 'into' as the two words in and to: a messenger (an angel, from the Greek for messenger) sitting inside the word to

explanation.surface: A courier makes a delivery of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'into' as 'in TO': the messenger, ANGEL, goes in the word TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Under fire, reportedly swapping parts of sense of style

indicators.note: swapping parts means the two halves of the word change places
reportedly means the word as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: panache is flamboyant confidence and style

explanation.surface: A stylish person is criticised by rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, panache sounds like PAN-ASH; 'swapping parts of' it puts the halves the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray that sits beneath a grate to collect ashes is found literally below the fire.

clue.text: It's worth putting money into apparently noisy alb

parts.note: something noisy has sound in it
an alb is a white linen vestment worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A loud priestly robe is offered as a good place to invest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags the whimsical reading: a noisy alb would be a vestment with sound in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe, reliable investment is one judged worth backing with cash.

clue.text: This is it!

parts.note: the word it is itself an example of the grammatical category being described

explanation.walkthrough: 'This is it!' sounds like an exclamation of excitement, but it means the word 'it' belongs to the category named.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as I, you, he and it stand in for people or things and are classed grammatically this way.

clue.text: President and Labour Minister of Health embraced the Queen twice

indicators.note: embraced means the minister's name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Aneurin 'Nye' Bevan was the Labour health minister who founded the NHS

indicators.note: twice means the royal abbreviation appears two times

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A president and a British health minister both embraced the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Nyerere was the first president of Tanzania.

clue.text: Definitely not right getting close to star of Lolita

indicators.note: not means the right abbreviation is to be left out

parts.note: surely means certainly, definitely
on can mean beside or near, as in a town on the river

explanation.surface: Someone is certainly not correct about getting near the star of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue Lyon played the title role in Stanley Kubrick's 1962 film of Nabokov's novel.
